"Yes, of course, but we cannot outrun them forever." a nervous squire said, chasing after Red until a vicious backhand sent him to the ground.

"We Ride." Red repeated, pointing out across the snow cloaked wastes towards the campfires of the enemy, his intentions clear. Squires and Knights began waking up at the sound of Red's raised voice, armor being gathered and horses warmed up. Red donned his ceremonial armor, the gleaming red metal for which he earned his name, the tall helmet that left his face bare, daring his enemies to strike, and the shield of the Core, bearing the symbol of their order, passed down for generations as they fought a losing battle against insatiable enemies.

"WE RIDE!" Red bellowed, the call to arms, the song of battle. Bootsteps resounded throughout the keep as final preparations were made, prayers to the forefathers muttered and blades sharpened. The Knights of The Core gathered for their final charge, knowing that they rode to their deaths, knowing that they would be unremembered and unmourned, but knowing that to die fighting was better than to die running.

Red trotted forward of the group and looked over his men, he felt pride swell in his heart as he saw not a single flicker of doubt or fear amongst them. These brave men would ride with him into the teeth of death, screaming defiance every step of the way, and he knew no speech would stir them to any greater heights of bravery or further firm their hands. With solemnity he drew his blade, took one deep breath, and bellowed loudly enough to wake the enemy forced many miles away WE RIDE!! and the Knights charged

What's the point of the index in the end of textbooks?
Its for finding references to keywords in the textbook. TBH, I never used the index in textbooks until in my undergraduate studies, I only began using them in my post graduate studies.
Thanks your answer was the only polite one. Yeah I'm an undergrad and I use digital copies of most books, so I just do ctrl+F. xD
That's also a good/easy way to find info. Unfortunately when I studied, I was unable to get digital copies of my textbooks.

Indexes are useful for finding specific keywords, and it holds a record for each time that specific keyword is mentioned so you can find all relevant information easier.

For example, if I'm looking for information on "photosynthesis", it might be mentioned on Page 1579, page 145, and page 223. The index will record each one of those, and let me find all the information about photosynthesis that there is, without having the look throughout the entire book for a few snippets of information.
